subject: Full Syllabus
summary: a mixed full-syllabus warm-up for the sixth full-length mock: antonyms, a clock that gains time, the inverse of a 2 × 2 matrix, Euler's method, uniformly accelerated rotation, strain energy in stepped bars, shear stress in rectangular beams, instantaneous centres, springs in series, the Soderberg criterion, laminar pipe flow, pin-fin efficiency, polytropic work, cold working and x̄ control charts

questions.text: Select the word that is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to TACITURN.
solution: Concept: 'Taciturn' describes a person who says very little.
Reserved, silent and sullen are all close to it in meaning, not opposite.
The opposite is talkative, option (B).
Exam tip: For antonym questions, first strike out every option that is a synonym; what remains is usually short.

questions.text: A wall clock gains 5 minutes every hour. It is set to the correct time at 8:00 a.m. When the correct time is 8:00 p.m. the same day, the clock shows
solution: Concept: A clock that gains at a steady rate is ahead by (gain per hour) × (hours elapsed).
From 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. is 12 hours, so the clock gains 12 × 5 = 60 minutes.
It therefore shows 9:00 p.m., option (B).
Exam tip: If the question gives the time shown by the faulty clock instead, the elapsed true time is (shown time)/(1 + gain fraction): here 65 clock minutes = 60 true minutes.

questions.text: The inverse of the matrix with rows (3, 1) and (5, 2) has rows
solution: Concept: For a 2 × 2 matrix with rows (a, b), (c, d): A−1 = (1/det A) × [rows (d, −b), (−c, a)].
So A−1 has rows (2, −1) and (−5, 3), option (A).
Exam tip: Check by multiplying: (3, 1)·(2, −5) = 1 and (3, 1)·(−1, 3) = 0, giving the first row of I.

questions.text: The equation dy/dx = 2x − y with y(0) = 1 is solved by Euler's (explicit) method with a step h = 0.1. The value of y at x = 0.2 (round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Euler's method: yn+1 = yn + h f(xn, yn).
Exam tip: Euler's method uses only the slope at the start of each step, so its error per step is of order h2 and the total error of order h.

questions.text: A wheel starts from rest and accelerates uniformly to 600 rpm in 10 s. The number of revolutions it makes in this time is ______
solution: Concept: With uniform angular acceleration from rest, the angle turned = average speed × time.
Final speed = 600 rpm = 10 rev/s; average speed = 5 rev/s.
Revolutions = 5 × 10 = 50.
Exam tip: The rotational equations mirror the linear ones: θ = (ω0 + ω)t/2, just as s = (u + v)t/2.

questions.text: Bars A and B, shown, are of the same material and length L. Bar A has a uniform diameter d. Bar B has diameter d over half its length and 2d over the other half. Both carry axial loads that produce the same maximum stress σ. The ratio of the strain energy stored in B to that stored in A is
solution: Concept: U = Σ P2Li/(2AiE); the load is fixed by the maximum stress in the thinnest part.
Both bars carry P = σA (A = πd²/4). U<sub>A</sub> = σ<sup>2</sup>AL/(2E).
U<sub>B</sub> = (P<sup>2</sup>/2E)[(L/2)/A + (L/2)/(4A)] = (σ<sup>2</sup>AL/2E)(1/2 + 1/8) = (5/8)U<sub>A</sub>; option (B).
Exam tip: Enlarging part of a bar lowers its energy-absorbing capacity for the same peak stress, which is why bolts for shock loads are turned down to the core diameter.

questions.text: A beam of rectangular section 120 mm wide and 240 mm deep carries a vertical shear force of 72 kN. The transverse shear stress at a level 60 mm above the neutral axis (in MPa, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: τ = VA′ȳ′/(Ib), which for a rectangle gives the parabola τ = (V/2I)(d2/4 − y2).
Average stress = V/(bd) = 72 000/28 800 = 2.5 MPa, so τ<sub>max</sub> = 1.5 × 2.5 = 3.75 MPa at the neutral axis.
Exam tip: Half-way from the neutral axis to the top fibre the shear stress is always 3/4 of its maximum in a rectangle.

questions.text: For a four-bar chain (including the fixed link), the total number of instantaneous centres and the number of them that lie at the pin joints are
solution: Concept: The number of instantaneous centres of n links is N = n(n − 1)/2.
Four of them (I12, I23, I34, I14) are at the pin joints and can be written down by inspection; the other two (I13, I24) are found with Kennedy's theorem: 6 and 4, option (D).
Exam tip: Of the four at the joints, I12 and I14 (on the frame) are fixed; I23 and I34 move with the links.

questions.text: A 5 kg mass hangs from two springs of stiffness 2 kN/m and 3 kN/m connected in series. The natural frequency of the system (in rad/s, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Springs in series: 1/keq = 1/k1 + 1/k2; ωn = √(keq/m).
Exam tip: In series the equivalent stiffness is always less than the smaller spring; in parallel the stiffnesses simply add.

questions.text: A machine part made of a steel with yield strength 300 MPa and corrected endurance limit 200 MPa carries a fluctuating stress with a mean of 100 MPa and an amplitude of 50 MPa. The factor of safety by the Soderberg criterion is about
solution: Concept: Soderberg line: σm/Syt + σa/Se = 1/N.
Exam tip: Soderberg (using Syt) is the most conservative of the common criteria; Goodman uses Sut and Gerber a parabola.

questions.text: Oil (density 900 kg/m³, dynamic viscosity 0.1 Pa·s) flows at 1 litre per second through a horizontal pipe of 40 mm diameter and 50 m length. Assuming fully developed laminar flow, the pressure drop over the length (in kPa, round off to one decimal place) is ______
solution: Concept: Hagen–Poiseuille: Δp = 128μLQ/(πD4), valid for laminar flow (Re below about 2000).
Exam tip: At a fixed flow rate Δp ∝ 1/D4 in laminar flow, so a small error in diameter gives a large error in pressure drop.

questions.text: An aluminium pin fin (k = 200 W/m·K) of 10 mm diameter and 100 mm length has an insulated tip, and h = 50 W/m²·K. The base is 80 K hotter than the surrounding air. The fin efficiency and the heat lost by the fin are about
solution: Concept: For an insulated-tip fin, ηf = tanh(mL)/(mL) with m = √(hP/(kA)) = √(4h/(kd)) for a pin.
Exam tip: Check with q = √(hPkA) θb tanh(mL): √(hPkA) = 0.157 W/K, so q = 0.157 × 80 × 0.762 = 9.6 W.

questions.text: Air is compressed in a closed cylinder from 100 kPa and 0.3 m³ to 0.1 m³ following pV<sup>1.3</sup> = constant. The work done on the air (in kJ, round off to one decimal place) is ______
solution: Concept: Polytropic boundary work: Wby = (p1V1 − p2V2)/(n − 1).
p<sub>2</sub> = 100 × 3<sup>1.3</sup> = 417.1 kPa; p<sub>2</sub>V<sub>2</sub> = 41.71 kJ and p<sub>1</sub>V<sub>1</sub> = 30 kJ.
Wby = (30 − 41.71)/0.3 = −39.0 kJ, so the work done on the air is 39.0 kJ.
Exam tip: For compression the polytropic formula gives a negative value of work done by the gas; read the question for the sign it wants.

questions.text: When a metal is cold worked (plastically deformed below its recrystallisation temperature),
opts: its strength and hardness rise while its ductility falls
its strength and ductility both rise
its hardness falls and its ductility rises
questions.ans: (A) its strength and hardness rise while its ductility falls
solution: Concept: Cold work multiplies dislocations, which tangle and obstruct one another (strain hardening).
Yield strength, tensile strength and hardness therefore rise, while elongation (ductility) falls; conductivity drops slightly.
So strength and hardness rise, ductility falls, option (A).
Exam tip: Annealing (recovery, recrystallisation and grain growth) reverses these changes.

questions.text: Samples of 5 parts each are taken from a process. The grand mean of the sample means is 50.00 mm and the average sample range is 4.00 mm. Taking A<sub>2</sub> = 0.577 for n = 5, the upper control limit of the x̄ chart (in mm, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: For an x̄ chart built from ranges, UCL = x̿ + A2R̄ and LCL = x̿ − A2R̄.
Exam tip: A2R̄ is a shortcut for 3σ/√n, with σ estimated as R̄/d2; A2 falls as the sample size grows.
